description: What a branch decided ON has to be the claim, not a record the claim was filed in. `/promote` compares `req.body.role` and picks the branch the caller asked for, which is the weakness. `/scope` builds `{ id, scope }` out of a field of the same kind and hands the object to a helper whose first line is a presence check on the object -- and the engine reported that as a security decision made on the caller's own claim. It is not one: nothing there reads a field, and the object travels wherever the record travels. medplum's is the measured case. `{ ...login, scope }` reached `if (input === null || input === undefined) return input` in an attachment-URL rewriter eight frames and three modules away, and the finding was reported HIGH and gating at a line where `req.body.scope`, the expression it named as the source, does not occur. The classification already refuses a value read OUT of a structure it reached; this is the same question asked the other way round, and both directions have to be refused for the answer to mean what it says.

expected.note: the branch runs because the caller said so, and this is the whole of the weakness; narrowing the rule must not reach it
